column1: # Baseline evidence digests for the CertiTherm refactor.
# `make reproduce-dev` on moe-server from a clean checkout of the commit below, BEFORE any
# THREE roles, not two. The first version of this file had only decision/provenance and was
# wrong: it classified results.tsv, plans.tsv and REPORT.md as decision, then the refactor
# run reproduced 27 of 30 and those three differed -- which reads as a failed equivalence
#   decision          -- physics and derived numbers with no dependence on wall clock:
#                        measurement_registry, spectral_envelopes. These MUST be bit-identical
#                        after a pure-move refactor, and were: 27 of 27.
#   provenance        -- receipts embedding git sha, host, timestamps, or a builder-source
#                        digest over a fixed file list. Extracting code out of experiments.py
#                        forces that list to change, so these are expected to differ and are
#   budget_dependent  -- results.tsv, plans.tsv and the report built from them. The exact
#                        synthesizer runs against a 1800 s wall-clock budget on a shared
#                        machine, so how many iterations fit is not reproducible. Compare the
#                        VERDICT and COST columns, which must be identical, and expect
#                        seconds, iteration counts, cut counts and the bounds derived from
# Measured for the refactor run at adb751d: every verdict and cost column identical --
# exact_status, exact_cost, all four policy statuses and costs, certified_upper_bound,
# unexpected_failure, interval_violation, candidate_order. The 18 columns that moved are
# wall-clock seconds and the search state a fixed budget reaches. One run got 41 iterations
# where the other got 40, and its lower bound was 11% better (92.2 vs 82.7) -- which is
# itself evidence that the bound is starved of well-chosen cuts, not evidence of a defect.
